/* DIVERGENCE(MVDM-HOST-DIV-460): ICW1 retires the PIC's pending
* and in-service ownership, but the original standalone reset did not
* notify the NT device EOI gates. Snapshot before clearing, then send
* their existing cancellation notification while the ICA critical section
* excludes a heartbeat/device race. A callback can publish a new request;
* that request is deliberately not part of this retired snapshot. */
#ifdef NTVDM
host_ica_lock();
canceled = asp->ica_irr | asp->ica_isr;
#endif
#ifdef NTVDM
if (canceled & (1 << i))
host_EOI_hook(i + (adapter << 3), -1);
host_ica_unlock();
#endif

initial_review: Three DIV460 additions implement ICW1 cancellation snapshot, device notifications and locking; original initialization assignments retained.
counter_review: IRR and ISR both lose ownership during ICW1. Original SWPIC_clear_int already uses -1 cancellation, distinct from normal EOI. Recursive IcaLock protects reset/callback against device producers. Notifications after reset preserve same-line callback requeue; union prevents duplicate cancellation when IRR and ISR share a bit. Reset remains controller-local.
evidence: nt_eoi.c:204 cancellation dispatcher and :366 Rtl critical section; timer.c:1896 clears EoiPending/EoiIntsPending on negative count; nt_mouse.c:2041 flushes canceled mouse events; keyba.c:2172 distinguishes cancellation from early EOI; cmosnt.c:344 RTC callback. test/mvdm-host/pic_reset_eoi_test.c exercises master/slave, IRR/ISR, repeat, requeue, AEOI empty state, real RTC/mouse hooks; keyboard_controller_pic_test.c covers keyboard cancellation.
limits: Source/test inspection only, not a fresh run. Fixture directly seeds some PIC states and stubs host dispatch/delay. AEOI test checks empty reset rather than end-to-end interrupt delivery. Cross-IRQ callback requeue into another still-pending cancellation bit is not covered; actual callback fanout must be checked before claiming arbitrary callback safety.
